written: 2026-10-03, before any GDELT data was downloaded or any outcome analysis
purpose: Collect a candidate list of news articles about accidents at plants, used only as a side check on accident dates and on accidents missing from RMP and NRC (plan Deviation D1). Every candidate is checked by hand before use.
fields_used: Only the GDELT batch time (DATE), the collection type, the website (SourceCommonName) and the article link (DocumentIdentifier or SOURCEURL). None of GDELT's machine-made themes, tone, locations, names or event codes are used.
how_words_are_matched: The article link is lower-cased, the website part is removed, and the rest is split into words at every character that is not a letter or digit. A word list entry matches a link word that starts with it. Entries with a space are phrases and must appear as consecutive words. Entries of three letters or fewer (tx, itc, tpc, lng, h2s) must match a whole word.
keep_rule: Keep the article if (B) it has an event word AND a facility word, or (C) it has an event word AND an industrial-town word. Each kept row records which of B and C matched, and whether a Texas place word or a Texas news website is present.

streams.gdelt2_gkg: data.gdeltproject.org/gdeltv2/*.gkg.csv.zip listed in masterfilelist.txt, 2015-02-18 to the download date (English stream; the separate translation stream is not used because its inclusion depends on machine translation)
streams.gdelt1_gkg_daily: data.gdeltproject.org/gkg/YYYYMMDD.gkg.csv.zip, 2013-04-01 to 2015-02-18 (only articles in which GDELT's software found a place; this inclusion bias is reported)
streams.gdelt1_events_daily: data.gdeltproject.org/events/YYYYMMDD.export.CSV.zip, 2013-04-01 to 2015-02-18, SOURCEURL field (only articles GDELT's software turned into an event; same caveat)

integrity: Each GDELT 2 file is checked against the MD5 in GDELT's master file list; every processed file is listed with its size, MD5, SHA-256 and rows kept.
